name: Firmus Project Southgate Stage 1 (Launceston AI Factory)

address.value: 23 Killafaddy Road and 66-92 St Leonards Road, St Leonards TAS 7250
address.note: Council agenda lists the address as '23 Killafaddy Road, 58, 66, 68 and 92 St Leonards Road, St Leonards'; 58 and 68 St Leonards Road are only for works inside drainage and electricity easements. Includes partial demolition of the existing data centre at 23 Killafaddy Road.

postcode.note: from the endorsed planning report title '23 Killafaddy Road & 66-92 St Leonards Rd TAS 7250' listed in the agenda

lat.note: Geocoded 2026-09-27 from '23 Killafaddy Road, St Leonards TAS 7250' with the ArcGIS World Geocoder (PointAddress, score 100). Cross-check: the OpenStreetMap building footprint ('Firmus LST01, 23, Killafaddy Road, Killafaddy, St Leonards, ') is 65m away.

builder.note: head contractor not named in the council documents or news coverage read

developer.note: applicant Pitt&Sherry on behalf of Firmus Technologies; one endorsed drawing is by Firmus Grid Pty Ltd

mw_it.note: w.media (read in full): 'Stage 1 ... will deliver a combined 90MW of AI infrastructure ... beginning with 44MW in Stage 1a and expanding to 90MW in Stage 1b. A further 300MW is planned in a future second stage, subject to approvals.' The source does not say whether this is IT or grid MW. The council agenda gives no MW figure.

mw_grid.note: ABC 15 Jun 2026: Firmus 'has signed a contract with state energy company Aurora for 104 megawatts to power the St Leonards AI factory'; w.media and ABC (Aug 2026) call it a '104MW'/'104-megawatt' AI factory

cost_aud_m.note: w.media: 'The $2.1 billion development'; Pulse Tasmania Jul 2026 says '$2 billion facility'. Not stated in the council agenda.

pathway.value: Development application under ss51 and 57 LUPAA 1993 (Tasmanian Planning Scheme - Launceston; Rural and Light Industrial Zones; use class Research and Development)
pathway.note: determined at a Special Council Meeting; public notification 2-18 Aug 2025

reference.note: 'DA0273/2025 - Research and Development - Demolition and construction of new data centre, including associated infrastructure and works within drainage and electricity infrastructure easements of 58 and 68 St Leonards Road'

lodged.note: lodgement date not stated in the agenda; Pitt&Sherry planning report Rev 00 is dated 24/06/2025

determined.note: minutes: permit granted, CARRIED 11:0 at the Special Council Meeting of 1 Sep 2025

jobs_construction.note: The Examiner (read in full): 'A Firmus spokesperson said there were about 80 workers on site, which would swell to 400 in the next couple of months.'

jobs_construction_other.note: The Examiner: 'More than 1000 workers (including off-site contractors) are expected to be involved in the project.' Lower bound.

jobs_operational.note: w.media: Firmus says it will be 'creating up to 100 direct jobs in its first stage'. Upper bound, and it conflicts with the lower figures below.

jobs_operational_other.note: council agenda: 'The maximum number of employees on site at any one time would be 30; regular shifts would be for 10 people.' (staff on site at one time, not a total headcount)
Firmus co-CEO Oliver Curtis (Pulse Tasmania 3 Jul 2026): ongoing employment of 'around half a full-time role per megawatt ... equating to about 52 jobs at St Leonards'

construction_start.note: started after approval on 1 Sep 2025 (w.media 3 Sep 2025: construction 'expected to begin shortly'); major earthworks complete and piling under way by early 2026 (source 3). Exact start date not found.

construction_end.note: expected. ABC 15 Jun 2026: 'expected to be operational early next year'. Earlier targets were mid-2026 (w.media Sep 2025) and end of 2026 (The Examiner).

open_questions: mw_it 90 MW (44 + 46) not stated as IT or grid
operational jobs conflict: up to 100 (Firmus launch) vs max 30 on site (DA) vs ~52 (Curtis)
